Subject: Post-call: SLO qualification & reproducibility plan

Hi Anna / Bob —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our end so we have alignment before we run any tests: 

Call highlights
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p50 overall latency ~50ms, p95 <= 200ms for single-turn generation. For streaming scenarios you called out a per-token first-byte target <= 20ms.
- Target steady-state throughput: ~200 requests/sec during peak events. Expected concurrency: 150–250 concurrent sessions.
- Workload shape: 60% short prompts (~20 tokens), 30% medium (100–200 tokens), 10% long (400+ tokens).

What we need from you to proceed
1) Canonical prompt set and representative payloads (examples of short/medium/long). Share via Drive/S3 link.
2) Clarify streaming semantics: full-duplex vs server-stream-only and whether you need incremental partial-turn scoring.
3) Any compliance constraints (PII redaction, VPC-only testing) and whether we need NDA in place before we pull data into our test harness.

Proposed Redwood benchmark approach (high level)
- Reproducible harness: we will run Redwood's eval harness (rdw-eval-harness repro-v2) with pinned commit and deterministic RNG seeds.
- Measurement definitions: cold-start vs steady-state runs, per-request latency (end-to-end), per-token streaming latency (first-byte and inter-token), and throughput saturation curves.
- Concurrency strategy: ramp to target concurrency in controlled steps (10–15% increments) and run 10-minute steady windows for each step.
- Data handling: we can accept sanitized prompt sets. For PII we recommend token-level redaction prior to upload.

Attachments: benchmark-checklist.pdf (high-level checklist).

Asks / next steps
- Please share the prompt set link + access (see Bob's notes on Ops availability).
- Sean (cc) will propose the exact measurement CSV and runner config.
- If you want to test on Dedicated capacity instead of hosted, flag now (we can provision a temporary reserved pool for the window).

I propose the following timeline: once we have prompts + access, 2 business days to stage harness + keys, then a 1-day execution window (streaming + non-streaming runs) and 1 day for reproducibility logs + report.

If that works, we can lock a window next week.

Thanks —
Soojin

Thanks Soojin —

This looks good and aligns with our notes. A couple of clarifications before we hand over the prompt bundle: 

1) Streaming measurements: when you say "first-byte and inter-token" latency, can you confirm whether "first-byte" is measured from request arrival or from model generation start? We need consistent definitions for our compliance team.

2) For long prompts (400+ tokens) we will want to understand how cached KV windows affect the steady-state numbers — can you include a run that demonstrates cold vs warmed KV cache?

3) Reproducibility: what artifacts will Redwood provide post-run? We require (a) raw request logs, (b) per-request token timings, (c) harness commit hash + runner config, and (d) a deterministic rerun recipe to replicate the 10-minute windows.

We are generally OK with sanitized prompt sets. I will coordinate with Ops on the redaction step; Bob may follow up with the S3 link.

Anna

Anna —

Short answers first: 
- "First-byte" is measured from request arrival at the Redwood ingress to the first chunk delivered to the client. For streaming we also report per-token inter-arrival (token-to-token) and model-side generation time. We will provide both client-observed and server-side timestamps to help you reconcile network variance.

- Cold vs warmed KV: we will run an explicit cold-start experiment (clear KV + cold worker spin-up) and a warmed-flow (populated KV cache). Each will have identical inputs to isolate the cache effect.

Artifacts we will provide (post-run)
1) Harness Git commit hash + runner config (JSON) + pinned RNG seed.
2) Raw request logs (timestamped) including full payload hashes — we redact any PII per your instructions.
3) Per-request per-token timing CSV (token_index, server_timestamp, client_timestamp, token_text_hash).
4) Repro script: a step-by-step script to re-run the exact window (container images, entrypoint flags).

Practical notes
- For streaming latency (per-token) you'll see some variance from network jitter; to reduce noise we recommend running 3 independent windows and reporting median-of-medians.
- If you need exact bitwise reproducibility of tokenization/hashes, we will pin tokenizer version/merges and include a tokenization dump.

Attaching the runner instructions we use internally (rdw_benchmark_harness_instructions.md). I'll also add our default measurement-definitions.csv to the run repo.

If you confirm the Drive/S3 links, we can provision ephemeral keys and a transient dedicated pool for the window if you prefer.

—Sean

1) Procurement/contract: we'll follow our standard Temporary Dedicated Trial addendum (1-week trial, limited SLA) and a short Data Processing Addendum for sanitized test data. I will drop that doc to legal@acmefinance.com by EOD.

3) Deliverables: post-run report (latency percentiles, throughput curves), raw logs + per-token CSV, harness commit and rerun script, and an archival reproducibility bundle (container images + runner config).

4) Measurements we will produce (summary)
- Per-run: p50/p90/p95 end-to-end latency (ms)
- Streaming: first-byte latency (ms), median inter-token latency (ms), tail token latency (p95)
- Throughput: achieved req/sec vs offered load, CPU/GPU utilization snapshots
- Repro: harness hash, RNG seed, and runner config

Attachments: measurement-definitions.csv, repro-checklist.txt

Next action items
- Bob: confirm S3/Drive access works for Redwood runner and legal NDA path if needed.
- Anna: confirm you want the cold vs warmed KV runs included (we'll default to include both).
- Sean: please create the runner PR with pinned commit and share the run config in the repo.

I'll send the Temporary Dedicated Trial addendum separately.
